title: Rule
description: One rule format for scoring, show/hide logic, section routing, workflow conditions and dashboard measures. A rule is a literal, a list of rules, or an operation: an object with exactly one key, the operator, whose value is its argument list. A value that isn't a list is a single argument, so {"var": "nps"} means {"var": ["nps"]}. A malformed rule is rejected; a well-formed rule never fails on unexpected data: arithmetic on a non-number gives null, comparing different types is false, a missing variable is null. Truthiness: false, null, 0, "" and [] are false, everything else is true. Equality is strict and deep: 1 equals 1.0, but "1" is not 1 and true is not 1. Rules are at most 32 levels deep and 1000 parts in all.

single.description: One argument: a rule that isn't a list, or a list holding just that rule.

var.description: Reads the data at a dotted path ("answers.nps", "items.0"); "" is the whole data. A second argument is the default when the value is missing or null.

and.description: True when every argument is truthy. Stops at the first falsy one. Always true or false.

or.description: True when any argument is truthy. Stops at the first truthy one. Always true or false.

not.description: True when the argument is falsy.

if.description: [condition, then, condition, then, ..., else]: the value after the first truthy condition, else the last argument when the count is odd, else null.

<.description: Less than, for two numbers or two strings (by code point, so ISO dates compare correctly). Three arguments test a < b < c. Different types: false.

<=.description: Less than or equal; three arguments test a <= b <= c (a range).

>.description: Greater than, for two numbers or two strings.

>=.description: Greater than or equal, for two numbers or two strings.

+.description: Sum of the arguments. Null if any isn't a number (strings are not converted).

-.description: a - b, or -a with one argument. Null for non-numbers.

*.description: Product of the arguments. Null for non-numbers.

/.description: a / b. Null when b is 0 or either isn't a number.

%.description: Remainder of a / b, with the sign of a. Null when b is 0.

round.description: Rounds half away from zero (2.5 to 3, -2.5 to -3) to 0–10 decimal places (default 0).

min.description: Smallest number. List arguments are spread out one level, so {"min": {"var": "scores"}} works. Null when there are none or any isn't a number.

max.description: Largest number, with lists spread out like min.

sum.description: Total of the numbers, with lists spread out like min. 0 when there are none.

avg.description: Mean of the numbers, with lists spread out like min. Null when there are none.

in.description: [needle, haystack]: text contains the needle (both strings), or a list holds a value equal to the needle.

any_of.description: [answer, options]: the answer (one value or a list, such as a multiple-choice answer) includes at least one of the options.

all_of.description: [answer, options]: the answer includes every one of the options. True for an empty option list.

length.description: Characters in a string (code points) or items in a list; null for anything else.

empty.description: True for null, "", [] and {}: an unanswered question.

lower.description: The string in lower case; null for non-strings.

days_between.description: [from, to]: whole days from one date to the other (negative when to is earlier). Each is an ISO date, YYYY-MM-DD, or a timestamp starting with one. Null for anything else.
